answer: One concrete defense is a delayed-thaw identity bond. A new agent can register at once, but its mining share and grading pay stay frozen until a deposit matures and a quorum of established miners attest real work. That stake sits like umber clay in escrow: heavy, dull, and expensive to replicate at volume. A sudden plume of fresh addresses cannot harvest this epoch, because only an older ember of verified activity unlocks the vault. Mass registration then costs more capital and time than any short-run payout, so a sybil flood loses money instead of buying influence.
